initial_plan.can_answer: partly: this can show annual counts of pedestrians reported injured in Brooklyn crashes, but not a population- or exposure-adjusted safety rate or all dimensions of road safety
initial_plan.denominator: none; annual count, not a rate
initial_plan.population: pedestrians reported injured in police-reported motor vehicle crashes whose borough is Brooklyn
filters: pedestrian injury count is present for summing
initial_plan.years: calendar years 2013 onward represented in the file; end year to be set after checking year coverage

data_check.rows_and_coverage: There are 483,501 Brooklyn crash rows dated 2013 onward, including 9,700 in 2026; 473,801 fall in 2013–2025. For each year 2013–2025 the observed dates reach Jan 1 and Dec 31, while 2026 runs only Jan 1–June 11.
data_check.field_quality: Borough values use uppercase spelling, so the Brooklyn filter is case-insensitive and trims whitespace. Among crashes dated 2013 onward, 668,406 have NULL borough, 0 have blank borough, 0 use checked unknown/unspecified labels, and 0 have a nonmissing borough outside the five NYC borough labels; NULL-borough rows cannot be assigned to Brooklyn. There are 0 Brooklyn-labeled rows with missing crash_date. The pedestrian-injury field is missing in 0 Brooklyn crash rows for 2013–2025.
data_check.decisions: Use the normalized Brooklyn match; exclude the partial 2026 year (9,700 rows) to avoid comparing an incomplete year; keep all otherwise eligible 2013–2025 rows since no injury fields are missing; do not assign NULL-borough crashes to Brooklyn.
data_check.plan_change: Set the final endpoint to 2025 after the data check identified 2026 as partial; normalize borough case/whitespace after finding uppercase category values.

final_plan.can_answer: partly: annual reported pedestrian-injury counts can indicate change in the recorded burden, but cannot establish exposure-adjusted risk or all dimensions of road safety
final_plan.metric: sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured per calendar year
final_plan.denominator: none; annual count, not a rate
final_plan.population: pedestrians reported injured in police-reported motor vehicle crashes labeled Brooklyn
filters: injury count is nonmissing; the data check found none missing
final_plan.limitations: Counts are not adjusted for pedestrian exposure or population; police-reported crashes with missing borough cannot be assigned, and 2026 is partial and excluded. The date range reaches both year boundaries in 2013–2025, but endpoint dates alone do not prove uninterrupted reporting.
